quests.coreMeaning: To look carefully at something.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Check' is a quick look (`check the time`). 'Inspect' means an official, thorough search for faults or safety.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Engineers will ___ every bridge cable after the storm.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — thorough official safety checks take 'inspect'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Engineers will inspect every bridge cable after the storm.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Let me ___ my pocket to see if I brought keys.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — casually checking pockets takes 'check', not formal 'inspect'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Let me check my pocket to see if I brought keys.

cousinWords.miniContext: Customs officers scan luggage carefully at the border.
Engineers will verify every bridge cable after the storm.
Audit marks the strongest tone in casual -> official.

quests.coreMeaning: To make an effort to do something.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Try' covers casual tasting or testing (`try this cake`). 'Attempt' highlights a serious effort at something tough.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Mountaineers will ___ to reach the peak before noon.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — bold, difficult efforts suit 'attempt'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Mountaineers will attempt to reach the peak before noon.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Let us ___ this spicy noodle soup for lunch.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — casual food tasting never sounds right with 'attempt'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Let us try this spicy noodle soup for lunch.

cousinWords.miniContext: Runners test to beat their personal best at the track.
Mountaineers will endeavor to reach the peak before noon.
Strive marks the strongest tone in casual -> serious.

quests.coreMeaning: To stop moving or acting for a time.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Wait' marks staying until someone arrives or an event starts. 'Pause' means briefly stopping mid-action to resume soon.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Hit the spacebar to ___ the movie while grabbing tea.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — temporarily stopping playback or speech is 'pause'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Hit the spacebar to pause the movie while grabbing tea.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Passengers had to ___ twenty minutes in the cold rain.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — staying at a stop uses 'wait', not 'pause'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Passengers had to wait twenty minutes in the cold rain.

cousinWords.miniContext: The speaker chose to hold briefly so people could clap.
Hit the spacebar to hesitate the movie while grabbing tea.
Delay marks the strongest tone in stop briefly -> stay.

quests.coreMeaning: Having little width or body weight.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Thin' applies to paper, ice, soup, or arms. 'Slim' praises an attractive lean figure or small chance.

makeovers.beforeSentence: They won the championship by a ___ lead of two points.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — lean figures or narrow margins sound better with 'slim'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: They won the championship by a slim lead of two points.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Do not skate on the ___ ice near the bank!
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — paper, soup, and ice sheets take 'thin', never 'slim'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Do not skate on the thin ice near the bank!

cousinWords.miniContext: There is only a lean chance of rain this afternoon.
They won the championship by a slender lead of two points.
Skinny marks the strongest tone in connotation shift.

quests.coreMeaning: Round and full in shape.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Fat' can sound blunt or refer to cooking oil. 'Plump' sounds warm and positive, especially for ripe fruit or pillows.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Choose ___ berries that feel firm and juicy.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — ripe fruit and cushions sound appetizing with 'plump'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Choose plump berries that feel firm and juicy.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Trim any white ___ off the steak before grilling.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — dietary cooking labels use 'fat', never 'plump'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Trim any white fat off the steak before grilling.

cousinWords.miniContext: Poultry farmers keep birds healthy and round on grain.
Choose chubby berries that feel firm and juicy.
Stout marks the strongest tone in blunt -> warm.

quests.coreMeaning: Measuring a great distance from bottom to top.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Tall' fits narrow vertical things like people, trees, and towers. 'High' fits mountains, ceilings, prices, and heights above ground.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Rent stays very ___ near the central train hub.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — levels, prices, mountains, and ceilings take 'high'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Rent stays very high near the central train hub.

makeovers.beforeSentence: My youngest brother grew almost six feet ___.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — people's height always uses 'tall', never 'high'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: My youngest brother grew almost six feet tall.

cousinWords.miniContext: Clouds drifted past the steep mountain ridge at sunrise.
Rent stays very lofty near the central train hub.
Towering marks the strongest tone in vertical objects -> levels.

quests.coreMeaning: To stop using one thing and take another.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Change' covers altering clothes, minds, or weather. 'Switch' means swapping cleanly between two choices or seats.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Would you mind if we ___ seats so friends sit together?
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — trading between two options or lanes takes 'switch'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Would you mind if we switch seats so friends sit together?

makeovers.beforeSentence: Mountain weather can ___ suddenly in October.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — gradual climate transformation uses 'change'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Mountain weather can change suddenly in October.

cousinWords.miniContext: Many drivers decided to swap to hybrid cars this year.
Would you mind if we alter seats so friends sit together?
Shift marks the strongest tone in alter -> trade.

quests.coreMeaning: To cause something to begin.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Start' covers engines, classes, and hobbies. 'Launch' means publicly introducing a product, ship, or major plan.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Engineers plan to ___ the new booking website on Friday.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — rolling out products or campaigns uses 'launch'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Engineers plan to launch the new booking website on Friday.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Turn the key right to ___ the cold engine.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — turning on cars or homework uses 'start'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Turn the key right to start the cold engine.

cousinWords.miniContext: The charity will begin its winter coat drive next week.
Engineers plan to open the new booking website on Friday.
Initiate marks the strongest tone in everyday -> public rollout.

quests.coreMeaning: To hold onto something for later.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Keep' means continue holding (`keep warm`). 'Save' emphasizes storing carefully so it is not lost or wasted.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Put foil over the cake to ___ it for tomorrow.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — preserving items against waste uses 'save'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Put foil over the cake to save it for tomorrow.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Can you ___ a promise and tell nobody yet?
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — holding a promise or secret takes 'keep', never 'save'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Can you keep a promise and tell nobody yet?

cousinWords.miniContext: Remember to store your boarding pass until exiting.
Put foil over the cake to hold it for tomorrow.
Reserve marks the strongest tone in hold -> protect.

quests.coreMeaning: Pleasant and considerate toward others.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Nice' is broad praise (`nice weather`). 'Polite' specifically praises respectful words and good manners.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Always stay ___ when asking strangers for directions.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — respectful manners use 'polite'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Always stay polite when asking strangers for directions.

makeovers.beforeSentence: We picked a ___ day for an outdoor picnic.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — weather or food cannot have manners ('polite').
makeovers.spokenSentence: We picked a nice day for an outdoor picnic.

cousinWords.miniContext: Shop staff sent a kind note apologizing for the wait.
Always stay courteous when asking strangers for directions.
Gracious marks the strongest tone in general -> manners.

quests.coreMeaning: Showing poor manners or disrespect.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Rude' sounds strong and emotional (`how rude!`). 'Impolite' is calmer and focuses on breaking social etiquette.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Some guests find checking texts at dinner slightly ___.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — mild etiquette breaks fit 'impolite'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Some guests find checking texts at dinner slightly impolite.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Waking to freezing water was a ___ surprise!
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — sudden shocks use the idiom 'rude awakening', not 'impolite'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Waking to freezing water was a rude surprise!

cousinWords.miniContext: Interrupting a speaker before they finish is blunt.
Some guests find checking texts at dinner slightly discourteous.
Disrespectful marks the strongest tone in mild -> harsh.

quests.coreMeaning: Satisfactory or morally solid.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Good' praises quality or morality. 'Decent' means solid, fair, and acceptable without being fancy.

makeovers.beforeSentence: For ten dollars, that corner diner serves a ___ lunch.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — good value and fair quality take 'decent'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: For ten dollars, that corner diner serves a decent lunch.

makeovers.beforeSentence: The puppy is very ___ at catching rubber balls.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — skill ('good at') never works with 'decent at'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: The puppy is very good at catching rubber balls.

cousinWords.miniContext: Every new worker deserves a solid salary and rest days.
For ten dollars, that corner diner serves a fair lunch.
Respectable marks the strongest tone in okay -> solid.

quests.coreMeaning: Feeling unhappy or troubled.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Sad' highlights sorrow or grief. 'Upset' mixes hurt feelings with mild frustration or shock.

makeovers.beforeSentence: She felt ___ when nobody told her the plan changed.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — hurt disappointment and frustration fit 'upset'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: She felt upset when nobody told her the plan changed.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Everyone cried during the ___ final scene.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — tearful tragedy takes 'sad', not annoyed 'upset'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Everyone cried during the sad final scene.

cousinWords.miniContext: He was visibly down after losing his grandmother’s ring.
She felt heartbroken when nobody told her the plan changed.
Distressed marks the strongest tone in mild -> deep sorrow.

quests.coreMeaning: Feeling strong displeasure.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Angry' fits serious writing and speech. 'Mad' is informal spoken English (`mad at me`), or British English for crazy.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Are you still ___ at me for eating your yogurt?
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — casual spoken frustration takes 'mad at'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Are you still mad at me for eating your yogurt?

makeovers.beforeSentence: Residents wrote ___ letters about the broken streetlights.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — formal reporting prefers 'angry', avoiding casual 'mad'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Residents wrote angry letters about the broken streetlights.

cousinWords.miniContext: Do not stay cross over a spilled cup of tea.
Are you still annoyed at me for eating your yogurt?
Furious marks the strongest tone in irritated -> furious.

quests.coreMeaning: Feeling fear or worry.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Scared' can go before nouns (`scared kids`). 'Afraid' follows verbs (`afraid of`), and also serves politely (`I'm afraid we're closed`).

makeovers.beforeSentence: I am ___ all tickets for tonight are sold out.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — polite bad-news phrasing always uses 'afraid'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: I am afraid all tickets for tonight are sold out.

makeovers.beforeSentence: The ___ kitten hid underneath the wooden sofa.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — directly before a noun ('kitten'), 'scared' works where 'afraid' cannot.
makeovers.spokenSentence: The scared kitten hid underneath the wooden sofa.

cousinWords.miniContext: Many young swimmers feel nervous of deep ocean water.
I am frightened all tickets for tonight are sold out.
Terrified marks the strongest tone in mild -> panic.

quests.coreMeaning: Not far away from a location.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Near' describes measurable closeness or prepositions (`near the park`). 'Nearby' sits smoothly before place nouns (`nearby shop`) without taking 'to'.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Stop at a ___ neighborhood bakery for warm soup.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — before a place noun or at sentence end, 'nearby' sounds natural.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Stop at a nearby neighborhood bakery for warm soup.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Station platforms sit ___ to the river bridge.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — 'near to' and 'close to' work smoothly, whereas 'nearby to' breaks grammar.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Station platforms sit near to the river bridge.

cousinWords.miniContext: Families appreciate having a close clinic during rainy winters.
Stop at a handy neighborhood bakery for warm soup.
Adjacent marks the strongest tone in preposition -> place noun.

quests.coreMeaning: Separated by a long space or time.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Far' asks simple distance (`how far?`). 'Distant' describes remote hills, forgotten memories, or cool behavior.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Tiny farmhouses stood on the ___ green hills.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — poetic or remote places before nouns use 'distant'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Tiny farmhouses stood on the distant green hills.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Is the railway station ___ from your apartment?
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — casual distance questions usually use 'far'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Is the railway station far from your apartment?

cousinWords.miniContext: A remote cousin mailed photos from across the ocean.
Tiny farmhouses stood on the isolated green hills.
Faraway marks the strongest tone in distance & tone.

quests.coreMeaning: Occupied with work or movement.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Busy' means packed with tasks or crowded traffic. 'Active' emphasizes energetic movement or live participation.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Grandma stays ___ by gardening and swimming daily.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — physical energy and participation use 'active'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Grandma stays active by gardening and swimming daily.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Wait a minute — the office phone line is still ___.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — occupied phones and schedules take 'busy', never 'active'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Wait a minute — the office phone line is still busy.

cousinWords.miniContext: Volunteers remain lively in cleaning the local riverbanks.
Grandma stays dynamic by gardening and swimming daily.
Swamped marks the strongest tone in movement -> overloaded.

quests.coreMeaning: Money required to pay for something.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Cost' includes total effort or living expenses (`cost of living`). 'Price' is the sticker amount on a shop item (`price tag`).

makeovers.beforeSentence: Look at the paper tag to check the jacket ___.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — shop tags show a specific 'price'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Look at the paper tag to check the jacket price.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Rising fuel bills increased the overall ___ of living downtown.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — the fixed phrase is 'cost of living', never 'price of living'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Rising fuel bills increased the overall cost of living downtown.

cousinWords.miniContext: Compare the ticket fee before booking your seat.
Look at the paper tag to check the jacket charge.
Expense marks the strongest tone in sticker -> overall harm.

quests.coreMeaning: Something given to honor winning or achievement.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Prize' is won in games, raffles, or contests. 'Award' honors formal merit, service, or film excellence.

makeovers.beforeSentence: The director won an international ___ for best editing.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — formal honor for career/art merit is an 'award'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: The director won an international award for best editing.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Lucky ticket forty won first ___ in the cake raffle!
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — game contests and lotteries give a 'prize', not a career 'award'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Lucky ticket forty won first prize in the cake raffle!

cousinWords.miniContext: Each science fair winner received a shiny gold gift.
The director won an international trophy for best editing.
Honor marks the strongest tone in game -> formal merit.

quests.coreMeaning: Work done to earn money.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Job' is a single paid position right now. 'Career' spans a person's long-term professional journey across years.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Dr. Patel built a twenty-year ___ in children’s medicine.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — decades of growth in one field form a 'career'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Dr. Patel built a twenty-year career in children’s medicine.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Fixing that loose kitchen hinge is a five-minute ___.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — tiny one-off tasks take 'job', never 'career'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Fixing that loose kitchen hinge is a five-minute job.

cousinWords.miniContext: Good mentoring helps interns start a strong post.
Dr. Patel built a twenty-year role in children’s medicine.
Vocation marks the strongest tone in task -> lifelong.

quests.coreMeaning: To discover where something is.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Find' covers lost keys and surprises (`find joy`). 'Locate' means pinpointing exact physical coordinates on a map.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Rescue helicopters tried to ___ the missing hikers.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — pinpointing coordinates takes 'locate'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Rescue helicopters tried to locate the missing hikers.

makeovers.beforeSentence: It took weeks to ___ time for relaxing together.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — abstract feelings or free time take 'find', never 'locate'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: It took weeks to find time for relaxing together.

cousinWords.miniContext: Use the mall map to spot the nearest elevator.
Rescue helicopters tried to discover the missing hikers.
Pinpoint marks the strongest tone in casual -> map pinpoint.

quests.coreMeaning: To be unable to find something.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Lose' can mean defeat (`lose a match`) or permanent loss. 'Misplace' means temporarily forgetting where you put an item.

makeovers.beforeSentence: I always seem to ___ my reading glasses inside the house.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — forgetting where you set an item down is 'misplace'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: I always seem to misplace my reading glasses inside the house.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Play focused defense so we do not ___ the finals!
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — sports games can only be 'lost', never 'misplaced'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Play focused defense so we do not lose the finals!

cousinWords.miniContext: Check the coat pocket whenever you drop your gloves.
I always seem to mislay my reading glasses inside the house.
Forfeit marks the strongest tone in temporary -> defeat.

quests.coreMeaning: To transport something to a destination.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Send' starts the journey from your hand. 'Deliver' completes handing it directly to the doorstep or listener.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Drivers ___ fresh groceries right to your porch.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — completing final drop-off takes 'deliver'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Drivers deliver fresh groceries right to your porch.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Please ___ me a text once your plane lands.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — hitting send on a phone uses 'send', not 'deliver'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Please send me a text once your plane lands.

cousinWords.miniContext: Florists promise to mail birthday roses before noon.
Drivers ship fresh groceries right to your porch.
Dispatch marks the strongest tone in send out -> arrive safely.

quests.coreMeaning: To set something in a position.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Put' fits casual everyday commands (`put it away`). 'Place' emphasizes careful, gentle, or deliberate positioning.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Carefully ___ the glass vase in the center of the shelf.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — gentle, careful positioning favors 'place'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Carefully place the glass vase in the center of the shelf.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Do not ___ all the blame on one new driver.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — fixed idioms like 'put the blame on' sound unnatural with 'place'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Do not put all the blame on one new driver.

cousinWords.miniContext: Waiters set fresh napkins beside every plate.
Carefully lay the glass vase in the center of the shelf.
Position marks the strongest tone in casual -> careful.

quests.coreMeaning: To take things from where they sit.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Pick' lifts individual fruit, flowers, or choices. 'Gather' brings many scattered items or people into one group.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Neighbors met outside to ___ dry leaves into bags.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — collecting scattered things together takes 'gather'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Neighbors met outside to gather dry leaves into bags.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Reach up to ___ one red apple from the branch.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — plucking a single apple takes 'pick', not 'gather'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Reach up to pick one red apple from the branch.

cousinWords.miniContext: Students stopped to collect shells along the quiet beach.
Neighbors met outside to assemble dry leaves into bags.
Harvest marks the strongest tone in single -> group.

quests.coreMeaning: To remove dirt.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Clean' covers dusting, sweeping, or wiping. 'Wash' specifically uses water and soap.

makeovers.beforeSentence: You should ___ mud off your jeans with cold water.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — cleaning with soap and water is 'wash'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: You should wash mud off your jeans with cold water.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Take a dry cloth to ___ dust from the bookshelf.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — dry dusting uses 'clean' or wipe, never 'wash'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Take a dry cloth to clean dust from the bookshelf.

cousinWords.miniContext: Always rinse fresh berries under cool running water.
You should scrub mud off your jeans with cold water.
Sanitize marks the strongest tone in dry -> water & soap.

quests.coreMeaning: To let others have part of something.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Share' covers feelings, stories, and room cleanly. 'Split' specifically divides costs, bills, or logs into halves.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Four friends decided to ___ the pizza bill evenly.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — dividing money or food cleanly into shares takes 'split'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Four friends decided to split the pizza bill evenly.

makeovers.beforeSentence: I cannot wait to ___ this exciting news with Grandma!
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — telling news or kindness takes 'share', never 'split'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: I cannot wait to share this exciting news with Grandma!

cousinWords.miniContext: Two roommates divide the monthly rent right down the middle.
Four friends decided to allot the pizza bill evenly.
Apportion marks the strongest tone in generous -> exact cut.

quests.coreMeaning: To become larger or higher.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Grow' applies to plants, kids, and habits. 'Rise' moves upward (`sun rises`, `dough rises`, `prices rise`).

makeovers.beforeSentence: Clouds glowed pink as the sun began to ___ over the bay.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — moving upward like sun, heat, or bread takes 'rise'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Clouds glowed pink as the sun began to rise over the bay.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Water daily so the young basil plants ___ healthy.
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — living plants 'grow' roots and leaves, they do not 'rise'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Water daily so the young basil plants grow healthy.

cousinWords.miniContext: Warm air causes the fresh bread dough to climb quickly.
Clouds glowed pink as the sun began to expand over the bay.
Soar marks the strongest tone in upward -> bigger.

quests.coreMeaning: To feel a desire for something.
quests.whyDifferent: 'Want' marks practical daily desires. 'Wish' covers hopes that feel hard, magical, or polite greetings (`wish you luck`).

makeovers.beforeSentence: We all ___ you safe travels on your flight.
makeovers.earVerdict: Natural — polite hopes and blessings always take 'wish'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: We all wish you safe travels on your flight.

makeovers.beforeSentence: Do you ___ extra cheese on your sandwich?
makeovers.earVerdict: Doesn't fit — ordering everyday items uses 'want', never 'wish'.
makeovers.spokenSentence: Do you want extra cheese on your sandwich?

cousinWords.miniContext: Travelers toss coins and hope for sunny skies ahead.
We all desire you safe travels on your flight.
Yearn marks the strongest tone in need -> dream.
